title: 02 — Data Engineering Glossary
html:
02 — Data Engineering Glossary

The one idea: most confusion in data teams is vocabulary confusion — two people using "partition", "job" or "real-time" to mean different things. This glossary pins down what each term means in everyday data engineering and Databricks use, with a concrete example where one helps.

How to use this glossary

  • Terms are grouped alphabetically. Where a term has a common synonym, it is listed under the name you are most likely to hear, with a pointer from the other name.
  • Where a word means different things in different contexts (a partition on disk vs a partition in Spark memory, a Spark job vs a Databricks job), both meanings are given.
  • Deeper treatment lives in the chapters: processing types in 03, storage in 04, modelling in 05, Spark in 06, Databricks in 07, Delta in 08, streaming in 09, operations in 10 and patterns in 11.

A

Term Meaning
Accumulating snapshot fact table A fact table with one row per business process instance (an order, a claim) that is updated as the instance passes milestones. Example: an order row with ordered_at, shipped_at, delivered_at columns filled in over time.
ACID Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — the guarantees that a set of writes either fully happens or not at all, leaves the data valid, does not see half-finished concurrent writes, and survives crashes. Delta Lake, Iceberg and Hudi bring ACID to files on object storage.
Adaptive Query Execution (AQE) A Spark feature that re-optimises a query plan during execution using real statistics from completed stages: it can merge small shuffle partitions, switch a sort-merge join to a broadcast join, and split skewed partitions. On by default in modern Spark.
Aggregation Collapsing many rows into fewer by grouping and applying functions like SUM, COUNT, AVG, MAX. Example: daily revenue per store from millions of sales lines.
Airflow (Apache Airflow) An open-source orchestrator where pipelines are Python-defined DAGs of tasks with schedules, dependencies and retries. Widely used to coordinate jobs across many systems.
Anti join A join that returns rows from the left side that have no match on the right. Example: customers who never placed an order. In Spark: df.join(other, "id", "left_anti").
Apache Arrow A language-independent, in-memory columnar format. It lets tools (Spark, pandas, Polars, DuckDB) exchange data without serialising row by row; PySpark uses it to speed up pandas conversions and pandas UDFs.
Append A write mode that only adds new rows and never changes existing ones. The safest and cheapest write, ideal for bronze and event data.
At-least-once A delivery guarantee where every record is processed one or more times: nothing is lost, but duplicates are possible after retries. Pair it with idempotent writes or deduplication to get effectively-once results.
At-most-once A delivery guarantee where every record is processed zero or one time: no duplicates, but data can be lost on failure. Rarely acceptable for business data.
Auto Loader A Databricks feature (cloudFiles source) that incrementally ingests new files as they land in cloud storage, tracking which files have been processed and supporting schema inference and evolution.
Autoscaling Automatically adding or removing worker nodes based on load, within a configured minimum and maximum.
Avro A row-oriented binary file and message format with an embedded (or registry-held) schema and well-defined schema evolution rules. Common for Kafka messages and landing zones.
Azure Data Factory (ADF) Azure's managed data integration and orchestration service: copy activities, connectors to many sources, and pipelines that can trigger Databricks jobs.

B

Term Meaning
Backfill Running a pipeline for historical periods it has not processed (or must reprocess), e.g. loading the last two years after a new table is created or a bug is fixed.
Batch processing Processing a bounded set of data in one run, usually on a schedule. Example: a nightly job that processes all of yesterday's orders.
BI (Business Intelligence) Tools and practices for reporting and dashboards over analytical data. Examples: Power BI, Tableau, Databricks SQL dashboards.
Bloom filter A compact probabilistic structure that answers "definitely not present" or "maybe present". Some file formats and engines use them to skip files or row groups when filtering on high-cardinality columns.
Broadcast join A join where the smaller table is copied in full to every executor so the larger table can be joined without shuffling it. Fast when one side is small (tens to low hundreds of MB).
Bronze / silver / gold The three layers of the medallion architecture. Bronze holds raw data as ingested; silver holds cleaned, deduplicated, conformed data; gold holds business-level aggregates and models ready for consumption.
Bucketing Pre-hashing rows into a fixed number of files by a column so later joins or aggregations on that column can avoid a shuffle. A Hive/Spark table feature; not supported for Delta tables, where clustering is used instead.
Business key The identifier the business uses for an entity, such as a customer number or ISBN. Synonym for natural key. Data Vault hubs are built on business keys.

C

Term Meaning
Cache / persist Keeping a computed DataFrame in executor memory (and/or disk) so repeated actions do not recompute it. cache() uses the default storage level; persist() lets you choose.
Cardinality The number of distinct values in a column. High-cardinality (user_id) vs low-cardinality (country). It drives choices of partition keys, clustering keys and join strategies.
Catalog (1) A metadata system that knows which tables exist, their schemas, locations and permissions. (2) In Unity Catalog, the top level of the three-level namespace catalog.schema.table.
Catalyst optimizer Spark's query optimiser: turns DataFrame and SQL code into a logical plan, applies rules (predicate pushdown, column pruning, constant folding), then chooses a physical plan.
CDC (Change Data Capture) Capturing inserts, updates and deletes from a source system as a stream of change events, instead of copying whole tables. Log-based CDC reads the database transaction log.
Change Data Feed (CDF) A Delta Lake feature that records row-level changes (insert, update pre-image and post-image, delete) for a table so downstream jobs can read just what changed.
Checkpoint (1) In streaming, the directory where a query stores its progress (offsets) and state so it can resume exactly where it stopped. (2) In Delta Lake, a Parquet snapshot of the transaction log written periodically so readers do not replay every JSON commit.
Clone (deep / shallow) Delta copies of a table. A deep clone copies data files and metadata; a shallow clone copies only metadata and points at the source's files. Useful for testing and backups.
Cloud object storage Cheap, durable, highly scalable storage of immutable objects addressed by key: ADLS Gen2, Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage. The foundation of data lakes and lakehouses.
Cluster A group of machines working together. In Databricks, a set of VMs with one driver and zero or more workers running Spark.
Cluster manager The component that allocates machines and resources to Spark applications (standalone, YARN, Kubernetes, or Databricks' own).
Coalesce Reducing the number of Spark partitions without a full shuffle, by merging existing partitions. Contrast with repartition, which shuffles.
Columnar storage Storing all values of a column together rather than all values of a row together. Analytical queries read only the columns they need and compress far better. Parquet and ORC are columnar.
Compaction Rewriting many small files into fewer larger ones to speed up reads. In Delta, done with OPTIMIZE or automatically with auto-compaction.
Compression codec The algorithm used to compress file data: snappy (fast, moderate ratio), zstd (good ratio, good speed), gzip (high ratio, slow, not splittable as a whole-file codec).
Conformed dimension A dimension shared with identical meaning and keys across several fact tables or data marts, so metrics can be compared. Example: one dim_date and one dim_customer used everywhere.
Cube A multidimensional pre-aggregated structure (measures by many dimensions) used for fast slicing. Also a SQL operator, GROUP BY CUBE(a, b), which produces aggregates for every combination of the listed columns.

D

Term Meaning
DAG (Directed Acyclic Graph) A graph of steps with directed dependencies and no cycles. Orchestrators model pipelines as DAGs of tasks; Spark models a query as a DAG of stages.
Data contract An explicit, versioned agreement between a data producer and its consumers covering schema, semantics, quality guarantees, freshness and change process.
Data lake A store of raw and processed data as files (often Parquet, JSON, CSV) in object storage, with schema applied at read time. Cheap and flexible, but without transactions it tends to rot into a data swamp.
Data mart A subject-focused subset of the warehouse built for one team or domain, e.g. a finance mart or marketing mart.
Data mesh An organisational approach where domain teams own and publish their data as products, supported by a self-serve platform and federated governance, instead of one central data team owning everything.
Data product A dataset (or set of tables, views, APIs) published by a team with a clear owner, documentation, quality guarantees and a stable interface, intended for others to consume.
Data quality The degree to which data is fit for use, usually measured along dimensions such as accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness and validity.
Data skew Uneven distribution of data across partitions, so a few tasks process far more rows than the rest and the job waits on them. Example: 40% of events have country = 'US'.
Data skipping Avoiding reading files whose min/max statistics show they cannot contain matching rows. Delta collects these stats automatically for the first columns of a table.
Data swamp A data lake with no catalog, ownership, quality or lifecycle management, where nobody trusts or can find anything.
Data vault A modelling method (Data Vault 2.0) built from hubs (business keys), links (relationships) and satellites (descriptive attributes with history). Designed for auditability and parallel loading of many sources.
Data warehouse A central analytical database with enforced schemas, optimised for SQL queries over integrated, historical data.
DataFrame A distributed table of rows with named, typed columns. The main Spark API; operations on it are optimised by Catalyst.
Dataset (Spark) A strongly typed version of the DataFrame available in Scala and Java. In Python, only DataFrames exist.
DBU (Databricks Unit) Databricks' unit of processing consumption, billed per second. The DBU rate depends on the compute type and tier; cloud VM costs are billed separately for classic compute and bundled for serverless.
Dead-letter queue (DLQ) A place where records that failed processing are sent so the pipeline can continue and someone can inspect or replay them later.
Deduplication Removing duplicate records, typically by keeping one row per key (latest by timestamp) using ROW_NUMBER() or dropDuplicates.
Degenerate dimension A dimension attribute stored directly on the fact table with no dimension table of its own. Example: an invoice number on a sales line fact.
Delete (hard vs soft) A hard delete removes the row; a soft delete marks it (is_deleted = true). CDC pipelines must decide how to propagate each.
Deletion vectors A Delta Lake optimisation that marks rows as deleted in a small side file instead of rewriting the whole Parquet file, making deletes, updates and merges much cheaper.
Delta Lake An open-source table format that adds a transaction log to Parquet files, giving ACID transactions, schema enforcement, time travel and efficient upserts. Default table format on Databricks.
Denormalisation Deliberately duplicating data (e.g. copying customer name onto every order row) to avoid joins at query time. Standard in analytical models.
Dimension A table of descriptive context for facts: who, what, where, when. Examples: dim_customer, dim_product, dim_date.
DLT / Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines Databricks' declarative pipeline framework, originally called Delta Live Tables and now Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines. You declare streaming tables and materialized views plus quality expectations; the framework manages dependencies, orchestration and incremental processing.
Driver The Spark process that runs your program, builds the plan, schedules tasks on executors and collects results. One per application.

E

Term Meaning
ELT (Extract, Load, Transform) Load raw data into the target platform first, then transform it there with its compute (usually SQL). The default in lakehouses and cloud warehouses.
ETL (Extract, Transform, Load) Transform data in a separate engine before loading it into the target. Historically common when warehouse compute was expensive.
Event Hubs Azure's managed event streaming service; it exposes a Kafka-compatible endpoint, so Spark's Kafka source can read from it.
Event time vs processing time Event time is when something actually happened (a timestamp in the record); processing time is when the pipeline handled it. Windows and business metrics should normally use event time.
Exactly-once Each record affects the output exactly one time, even across failures and retries. In practice achieved end to end by combining replayable sources, checkpointed progress and idempotent or transactional sinks.
Executor A worker JVM process in Spark that runs tasks and holds cached data. A cluster has many executors.
Expectation A declarative data-quality rule in Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (e.g. amount > 0), configured to keep and record, drop, or fail on violating rows.
Explode Turning an array or map column into multiple rows, one per element. explode(col("items")).
External table A table whose data files live in a location you manage; dropping the table removes only the metadata. Contrast with managed table.

F

Term Meaning
Fact table A table of measurable business events or states at a declared grain, with foreign keys to dimensions and numeric measures. Example: fact_sales with quantity and amount per order line.
Factless fact table A fact table with keys but no numeric measures, recording that something happened (student attended class) or could have happened (product on promotion).
Feature store A system for defining, storing, sharing and serving ML features consistently between training and inference, usually with point-in-time correct lookups. In Databricks, feature tables are Unity Catalog tables with a primary key.
File skipping See Data skipping.
foreachBatch A Structured Streaming sink that hands each micro-batch to your function as a normal DataFrame, so you can run arbitrary batch logic such as a Delta MERGE.
Freshness How recently data was updated relative to expectation. A table that should update hourly but last updated six hours ago is stale.
Full load Reloading the entire source dataset each run and replacing the target. Simple and self-correcting, but costly for large tables.

G

Term Meaning
Gold layer The medallion layer of curated, business-ready tables: dimensional models, aggregates, feature tables.
Governance The policies and controls that decide who can access which data, how it is classified, how long it is kept and how its use is audited.
Grain The precise meaning of one row in a fact table. Example: "one row per order line per day". Declaring the grain is the first step in dimensional design.
Grouping sets A SQL feature to compute multiple GROUP BY combinations in one query (GROUPING SETS, ROLLUP, CUBE).

H

Term Meaning
High-watermark The largest value (timestamp, sequence id) already processed by an incremental load; the next run reads only rows above it.
Hive metastore The metadata service from Apache Hive storing table definitions and locations. Legacy Databricks workspaces use a per-workspace Hive metastore; Unity Catalog replaces it with a governed, account-level catalog.
Hot / warm / cold data Tiers by access frequency. Hot data is queried constantly and kept on fast, costly storage; cold data is rarely read and archived on cheap storage.
Hub A Data Vault table holding the unique list of business keys for one core entity (e.g. customer numbers), with a hash key, load date and record source.
Hudi (Apache Hudi) An open table format focused on record-level upserts and incremental pulls, with copy-on-write and merge-on-read table types.

I

Term Meaning
Iceberg (Apache Iceberg) An open table format with a metadata tree (metadata files, manifest lists, manifests) over data files, supporting ACID, hidden partitioning, partition evolution and time travel. Broad multi-engine support.
Idempotency A property of an operation where running it more than once has the same effect as running it once. The most important property of any pipeline task.
Incremental load Processing only new or changed data since the last run, using a high-watermark, CDC or file tracking.
Ingestion Bringing data from sources into the platform, as batches or streams.
Inmon Bill Inmon's approach: build a normalised, enterprise-wide warehouse first, then derive dimensional data marts from it. Often contrasted with Kimball's bottom-up dimensional approach.
Isolation level How concurrent transactions see each other. Delta Lake supports WriteSerializable (default) and Serializable.

J

Term Meaning
JDBC The Java database connectivity standard. Spark reads from and writes to relational databases through JDBC; parallel reads need a partition column and bounds.
Job (Databricks) A scheduled or triggered unit of orchestration in Databricks Workflows (Lakeflow Jobs), made of one or more tasks with dependencies.
Job (Spark) The work Spark runs for one action (count, write, collect). A Spark job is split into stages, and stages into tasks.
Join types Inner (matching rows only), left/right outer (all rows from one side plus matches), full outer (all rows from both), left semi (left rows that have a match, left columns only), left anti (left rows with no match), cross (every combination).

K

Term Meaning
Kafka (Apache Kafka) A distributed, durable, partitioned log used as an event streaming platform. Producers append to topics; consumers read at their own offsets and can replay.
Kappa architecture A design where all processing, including reprocessing, runs through a single streaming path; history is rebuilt by replaying the log.
Kimball Ralph Kimball's dimensional modelling methodology: business-process-focused star schemas with conformed dimensions, built incrementally.

L

Term Meaning
Lakehouse An architecture that combines the low-cost open storage of a data lake with warehouse features (ACID, schemas, governance, fast SQL) via an open table format.
Lambda architecture A design with two paths: a batch layer that recomputes accurate results over all data, and a speed layer that provides low-latency approximate results; a serving layer merges them. Costly because logic is duplicated.
Late-arriving data Records that arrive after the window or batch they belong to (by event time) has already been processed. Handled with watermarks, reprocessing windows or merges.
Late-arriving dimension A fact that arrives before its dimension row exists. Common fix: insert a placeholder ("inferred member") dimension row and update it when the real data arrives.
Lazy evaluation Spark builds a plan from transformations and only executes when an action requires a result, which lets it optimise the whole plan.
Lineage A record of where data came from and how it was transformed: table-to-table and column-to-column dependencies. Unity Catalog captures lineage automatically for queries it runs.
Link A Data Vault table recording a relationship between two or more hubs (e.g. customer placed order).
Liquid clustering A Delta Lake data layout technique that incrementally clusters data by chosen keys without fixed partitions, and lets you change the keys later without rewriting the whole table. Recommended by Databricks for new tables over partitioning plus Z-ordering.

M

Term Meaning
Managed table A table whose data location is managed by the catalog; dropping the table deletes the data (in Unity Catalog, after a retention period).
Materialised view A view whose result is stored and refreshed, so queries read precomputed data. In Databricks, materialized views are refreshed by a pipeline, incrementally where possible.
Medallion architecture Organising lakehouse data into bronze (raw), silver (clean, conformed) and gold (business-ready) layers, each built from the one before.
Merge / upsert An operation that updates rows when a key matches and inserts them when it does not (optionally deleting). MERGE INTO in Delta and SQL.
Metadata Data about data: schemas, owners, descriptions, file locations, statistics, lineage, tags.
Metastore The top-level container for metadata. In Unity Catalog, one metastore per region holds catalogs and is attached to workspaces.
Micro-batch Processing a stream as a series of small batches, each covering the data that arrived since the last one. Structured Streaming's default execution mode.
MLflow An open-source platform for the ML lifecycle: experiment tracking, model packaging, model registry and deployment. Managed and integrated with Unity Catalog in Databricks.

N

Term Meaning
Narrow transformation See Wide vs narrow transformation.
Natural key A key that comes from the source or the business domain (email, order number). Can change or be reused, which is why warehouses add surrogate keys.
Normalisation Structuring a relational schema to remove redundancy (1NF, 2NF, 3NF), so each fact is stored once. Good for OLTP writes; causes many joins for analytics.
Notebook An interactive document of code and markdown cells. Great for exploration; production logic should be in version-controlled, tested code even if run from notebooks.

O

Term Meaning
OBT (One Big Table) A fully denormalised wide table containing a fact and all its dimension attributes, so consumers never join. Simple for BI, costly to maintain when dimensions change.
Offset A consumer's position in a stream partition (Kafka offset, Event Hubs sequence number). Streaming checkpoints store offsets.
OLAP Online Analytical Processing: large scans and aggregations over historical data.
OLTP Online Transaction Processing: many small, concurrent reads and writes of individual records.
OPTIMIZE The Delta Lake command that compacts small files into larger ones and, when requested or configured, clusters data (Z-order or liquid clustering).
Orchestration Scheduling and coordinating pipeline tasks: order, dependencies, retries, parameters, alerts.
ORC Optimized Row Columnar: a columnar file format from the Hive ecosystem, similar in purpose to Parquet.
Output mode How a streaming query writes results: append (only new final rows), update (changed rows), complete (the whole result every time).

P

Term Meaning
Parquet The standard open columnar file format for analytics: column chunks grouped in row groups, per-column encoding and compression, and min/max statistics in the footer.
Partition (storage) A physical subdivision of a table into directories by column value, e.g. .../event_date=2026-09-01/. Lets queries skip whole directories.
Partition (Spark) A chunk of a distributed dataset processed by one task. The number of partitions sets the parallelism of a stage.
Partition pruning Skipping partitions (directories) that cannot contain matching rows, based on the query's filter on the partition column. Dynamic partition pruning does this using values from the other side of a join.
Periodic snapshot fact table A fact table recording the state of something at regular intervals. Example: account balance per account per day end.
Photon Databricks' native, vectorised query engine written in C++, compatible with Spark APIs, that speeds up SQL and DataFrame workloads. Enabled by default on SQL warehouses and serverless; optional on classic clusters.
PII Personally Identifiable Information: data that can identify a person (name, email, national ID, IP address). Requires classification, access control and often masking.
Pivot Turning distinct values of a column into separate columns, e.g. one column per month.
Predicate pushdown Moving filters as close to the data as possible: into the file reader (using Parquet statistics) or into the source database (a WHERE in the JDBC query), so less data is read.

Q

Term Meaning
Quarantine table A table where rows that fail quality checks are written, with the reason, instead of silently dropping them or failing the whole pipeline.

R

Term Meaning
RDD (Resilient Distributed Dataset) Spark's original low-level API: an immutable, partitioned collection with lineage for recomputation. It has no schema and bypasses Catalyst, so DataFrames are preferred.
Repartition Redistributing a Spark DataFrame into a given number of partitions (optionally by column) via a full shuffle.
Reprocessing Re-running a pipeline over data already processed, because of a logic change or bug fix. Requires idempotent writes to avoid double counting.
Retention How long data (or table history) is kept before deletion; driven by cost, regulation and business need.
Reverse ETL Syncing modelled data from the warehouse or lakehouse back into operational tools such as a CRM or marketing platform.
Row filter / column mask Unity Catalog fine-grained controls: a row filter function limits which rows a user sees; a column mask function returns a masked value for unauthorised users.
Row-oriented storage Storing all columns of a row together. Efficient for reading or writing whole records (OLTP, Avro); inefficient for scanning a few columns.

S

Term Meaning
Salting Adding a random suffix to a skewed join or grouping key to spread a hot key across many partitions, then combining the partial results.
Satellite A Data Vault table holding descriptive attributes for a hub or link, with history tracked by load date and a hash diff.
SCD (slowly changing dimension) Techniques for handling changes to dimension attributes over time. The common types follow below.
SCD type 0 Retain original: the attribute never changes after first load (e.g. original sign-up date).
SCD type 1 Overwrite: the new value replaces the old one; no history is kept.
SCD type 2 Add a new row: each change creates a new version with effective-from/to dates and a current flag, preserving full history.
SCD type 3 Add a column: keep the current value and one previous value (e.g. current_region, previous_region).
SCD type 4 Split rapidly changing attributes out of the main dimension. In Kimball's terms a mini-dimension; many teams use the term for keeping current rows in one table and history in a separate history table.
SCD type 6 A hybrid of types 1, 2 and 3 (1+2+3=6): type 2 rows for history plus a current-value column overwritten on every row of that entity.
Schema drift Unplanned changes to a source's structure: new columns, removed columns, changed types.
Schema enforcement Rejecting writes whose schema does not match the table (unknown columns, incompatible types). Delta does this by default.
Schema evolution Allowing a table's schema to change in controlled ways, e.g. adding new columns automatically with mergeSchema.
Schema registry A service storing versioned schemas for stream messages (Avro, Protobuf, JSON Schema) and checking compatibility between versions.
Semantic layer A layer that defines business metrics and dimensions once (e.g. "net revenue") so every tool computes them the same way.
Semi join A join returning left rows that have at least one match on the right, without duplicating them or adding right columns. "left_semi" in Spark.
Session window A window that groups events by activity, closing after a gap of inactivity, so window length varies per key.
Serverless compute Compute that the platform provisions and manages for you, starting in seconds, billed only for use; you do not choose VM types.
Shuffle Redistributing data across executors over the network so rows with the same key end up in the same partition. Needed for joins, groupBy and distinct; usually the most expensive part of a Spark job.
Silver layer The medallion layer of cleaned, validated, deduplicated and conformed data, usually modelled around business entities.
Sliding window A fixed-size window that advances by a smaller slide, so windows overlap and one event can belong to several. Example: 10-minute windows every 5 minutes.
Slowly changing dimension See SCD.
Small files problem Too many small files in a table, causing slow reads from per-file overhead and metadata pressure. Fixed by compaction and better write sizing.
Snowflake schema A dimensional model where dimensions are normalised into sub-dimensions (product → category → department). Saves storage, costs joins. Not to be confused with the Snowflake company.
Spark (Apache Spark) A distributed processing engine for large-scale data, with SQL, DataFrame, streaming and ML APIs. The compute engine of Databricks.
Spill When a Spark task's data does not fit in execution memory, it writes intermediate data to local disk. Visible in the Spark UI; a sign of under-partitioning or skew.
SQL warehouse Databricks compute optimised for SQL and BI workloads (classic, pro or serverless), with Photon enabled.
Stage / task A Spark job is split into stages at shuffle boundaries; each stage is split into tasks, one per partition, which run in parallel on executors.
Star schema A dimensional model with a central fact table directly joined to denormalised dimension tables, shaped like a star.
State store Where Structured Streaming keeps state between micro-batches for stateful operations (aggregations, deduplication, joins). RocksDB-backed state stores handle large state.
Streaming Continuously processing unbounded data as it arrives.
Streaming table In Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines and Databricks SQL, a Delta table that is fed incrementally by a streaming query and processes each input record once.
Structured Streaming Spark's streaming engine, which treats a stream as an unbounded table and lets you use the DataFrame API over it, executed as micro-batches by default.
Surrogate key A system-generated key (integer, hash) with no business meaning, used as the primary key of a dimension so history versions and source changes can be handled.

T

Term Meaning
Table format (open) A specification for managing a set of data files as a table: transaction log or metadata, schema, partitioning, snapshots. Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg and Apache Hudi.
Time travel Querying a table as it was at an earlier version or timestamp. SELECT * FROM t VERSION AS OF 12. Limited by log and file retention.
Transaction fact table A fact table with one row per discrete event at the lowest grain, e.g. one row per payment. The most common fact type.
Trigger In Structured Streaming, what starts each micro-batch: a fixed interval (processingTime), process all available data then stop (availableNow), or the experimental continuous mode.
Tumbling window A fixed-size, non-overlapping time window: 00:00–00:05, 00:05–00:10. Each event belongs to exactly one window.

U

Term Meaning
UDF (User-Defined Function) A custom function applied to columns. Python UDFs are opaque to the optimiser and add serialisation cost; prefer built-in functions, or vectorised pandas UDFs when needed.
Unity Catalog Databricks' unified governance layer: one metastore per region with catalogs, schemas, tables, views, volumes, functions and models, with centralised permissions, auditing and lineage.
Upsert Update-or-insert. See Merge / upsert.

V

Term Meaning
VACUUM The Delta Lake command that permanently deletes data files no longer referenced by the table and older than the retention threshold (default 7 days). Limits how far back time travel can go.
Vectorised execution Processing batches of column values per operation instead of one row at a time, making good use of CPU caches and SIMD. Photon and Arrow-based engines work this way.
Volume A Unity Catalog object for governing non-tabular files (images, PDFs, CSV drops) in cloud storage, addressed as /Volumes/catalog/schema/volume/path.

W

Term Meaning
Watermark In streaming, a moving threshold of event time (max event time seen minus an allowed delay) behind which data is considered too late. It lets Spark finalise windows and drop old state.
Wide vs narrow transformation A narrow transformation (filter, select, withColumn) computes each output partition from one input partition. A wide transformation (groupBy, join, distinct) needs data from many partitions and causes a shuffle.
Window function A SQL function computed over a set of rows related to the current row without collapsing them: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY ts DESC).
Workflow / job A Databricks orchestration unit (Workflows, now Lakeflow Jobs) of tasks such as notebooks, Python scripts, SQL, pipelines or dbt, with dependencies, schedules, retries and notifications.
Write-audit-publish (WAP) Writing new data to a staging area or branch, running quality checks on it, and only then making it visible to consumers.

Z

Term Meaning
Z-ordering A Delta layout technique (OPTIMIZE ... ZORDER BY (col)) that co-locates related values across files using a space-filling curve, improving data skipping on those columns. Largely superseded by liquid clustering for new tables.

Easily confused pairs

Pair The difference in one line
Partition (storage) vs partition (Spark) Directory on disk vs chunk of data handled by one task in memory
Spark job vs Databricks job One action's execution vs a scheduled orchestration unit
Checkpoint (streaming) vs checkpoint (Delta log) Stream progress and state vs a Parquet snapshot of the transaction log
Repartition vs coalesce Full shuffle to any count vs cheap merge to fewer partitions
Merge vs upsert Upsert is the behaviour; MERGE is the SQL statement that implements it (and can also delete)
Watermark (streaming) vs high-watermark (batch) Lateness threshold for event time vs last processed value for incremental loads
Materialised view vs streaming table Recomputed or incrementally refreshed query result vs append-style incremental ingestion table
Data lake vs lakehouse Files without transactions vs files plus a table format with ACID and governance
